answer: Each epoch the island registry auctions only 100 new identity slots, listed in a public atlas. An identity posts a key-bound bid bond to claim a slot; winners pay their bid, losers gain no slot. Honest applicants bid 40 credits, so one honest identity costs 40. An attacker drives a bidding spiral: the k-th fake slot costs 40+3(k-1) credits. For 1,000 fakes the total is about 1,538,500 credits, each slot still needing a distinct key-bound record in the atlas. A rented-bid ring fails: the atlas binds each bid to one key, so auditors void reused keys and burn the bond.
